## FRANCISCAN ORDER

one of the largest religious orders in Christendom, was founded by *St. Francis Seraphicus of Assisi* <note>The title "Seraphicus" refers to St. Francis's mystical vision of a seraph (a high-ranking angel) during which he received the stigmata.</note>, approved by *Innocent III* at the *Lateran Council* in the year 1215, and confirmed by *Honorius* in the year 1223. This order has produced several Popes, many Cardinals, Bishops, prominent prelates, and writers. Even the founders <note>Likely referring to the early governing bodies of the order</note> divided this order into three parts, namely:

First, that of the *Friars Minor* <note>original: "Minnebroeders," literally "Brothers of Love," the standard Dutch term for the Franciscan Ordo Fratrum Minorum</note>, which consists of various congregations of men, such as (1) those who are properly called *Friars Minor*, though commonly known as *Franciscans*; in this congregation, the continuous succession of the *Generalship* <term>Generalship: The office of the Superior General, the highest-ranking leader of the entire religious order</term> of the whole order has remained from its founder until today. This group currently includes the *Observants*, *Reformists*, *Discalced* <term>Discalced: From the Latin for "unshod," referring to monks or nuns who went barefoot or wore only sandals as a sign of poverty</term>, and *Recollects*. In former times, there were also reforms within this group known as the *Caesarines*, *Clareni*, *Amadeans*, *Narbonensians*, *Collectani*, *of the Holy Gospel*, or the *Capucio* and several others, which flourished until the time of *Leo X*; however, they were brought under the *Observants* by him in the year 1517 through the bull *Unionis; ite & vos in Vineam &c.* <note>Latin: "The Union; go ye also into the Vineyard, etc." This bull sought to unify the fractured branches of the Franciscan order.</note>. To these also belong the *Cloistered Brothers*, the *Brothers of Communion*, or the *Old Conventuals*. (2) The Dispensed *Friars Minor*, which

### G.

**GUILLEMITES**, a spiritual brotherhood who are also called ***White Mantles*** <note>original: *witte Mantels*; so named because of the color of their habit.</note> or ***Willemites***. This brotherhood follows the Rule of **St. Augustine**. **Albert**, **Renald**, or as others say, **John the Good of Mantua** governed and expanded this institution after the death of **St. William** (or **Willem**), who is said to have founded it. *Sabellicus, Onuphrius, Genebrardus.*

## H.

**HUMILIATI** <note>The "Humble Ones."</note>, a monastic order founded by certain *Milanese Nobles* in the 12th century; for when Emperor *Henry IV* had exiled some *Milanese* to *Germany*, others joined them in the year 1187 after *Cremona*, *Tortona* <note>The OCR reads "Torteua," likely a transcription error for the Italian city of Tortona.</note>, and *Milan* were devastated by *Frederick Barbarossa*. *John of Meda* <note>original: *Johannes van Meda*</note> was one of those who labored most in the year 1180 to establish this Order, and it was confirmed by the Papal See in the year 1200. When, in the 16th century, *Charles Borromeo* <note>original: *Karel Borromeus*; a prominent Archbishop of Milan and a leading figure of the Counter-Reformation.</note>, their protector, noticed many of their abuses—namely, that in 90 monasteries there were no more than 170 Brothers—he concerned himself with reforming them. However, he was shot <note>The original Dutch text says "doodgeschooten" (shot dead), though historically Borromeo survived this 1569 assassination attempt by a member of the order.</note> by one named *Hieronymus Donatus Farina* at the instigation of the Order. This caused Pope *Pius V* to abolish this entire Order in the year 1570 and distribute their assets to certain Cardinals who had little income. In the time of Pope *Innocent III*, there were certain heretics also called *Humiliati*, but these were condemned by him. *Chronicle of Ursperg; Ludovico Cavitelli’s Annals of Cremona; Giuseppe Ripamonti’s History of Milan, book 12; Spondanus at the year 1199; De Thou, book 1; Godeau, book 1.*

# JE

They are also called *Scholastics* <note>original: *Scholasticie*</note>, or *Students*, for they are distinguished by their dress, wearing a sleeved garment over their cassock, just as the *Students* in *Paris* used to wear during the time of *Ignatius Loyola* <note>The founder of the Society of Jesus (1491–1556)</note>. It is also worth noting that no one is easily admitted into their Society unless he possesses extraordinary mental gifts, is wealthy in means, or is of high birth. The *Jesuits* were banished from *France* in the year 1598 by a decree of the *Parliament of Paris*, being accused of having incited *Jean Châtel* <note>original: *Jan Castel*; a student of the Jesuits who attempted to assassinate King Henry IV in 1594</note> to murder King *Henry IV*. Indeed, in memory of this banishment, a *Pyramid* with a very biting inscription was erected at the great gate of the *Louvre*, which remained there until their restoration in the year 1605. In *England*, Queen *Elizabeth* likewise issued a sharp Edict against the *Jesuits* in the year 1602, which was later renewed under the reign of King *James I* <note>original: *Jacob I*</note> after the discovery of the Gunpowder Plot <note>original: *buschkruid verraad*; the 1605 conspiracy to blow up the House of Lords</note>, so that they all had to flee the country. A similar misfortune befell them in the year 1605 in the Republic of *Venice*. In the year 1607 in the *Kingdom of Poland*, and in the year 1619 in *Bohemia*, *Silesia*, *Moravia*, and *Hungary*, although they afterwards obtained much more prestige and wealth in those places. *Thuanus* <note>Jacques Auguste de Thou (1553–1617), a French historian and statesman</note> reports that in the year 1604 Pope *Clement VIII* was also set against them, because some *Jesuits* presumed to claim that it was not an Article of Faith that the Pope was the rightful

...successor of *St. Peter* was, and that one could confess through letters to a priest in another place, and it would have ended very badly for them, were it not that the Ambassador of the King of *Portugal* had spoken for them before the Pope. The *Jesuits* have until now always been at odds with other orders in the *Roman Church*, as for example with the followers of *St. Thomas* <note>The Thomists, primarily the Dominicans who followed the theology of Thomas Aquinas</note>, or the *Dominicans*, and *Jansenists* <note>A Catholic theological movement emphasizing original sin and divine grace, often opposed to Jesuit "laxity"</note>, who accuse them of *Pelagianism* <note>The belief that human beings can take the first steps toward salvation by their own efforts, without divine grace</note>, while the *Jesuits* in turn reproach them for being *Manichaeans* <note>An ancient dualist sect; used here as a slur for those they believed denied human free will</note> and proponents of *absolute predestination* <note>The doctrine that God has unalterably determined the fate of every soul</note>. The *Jesuits* also dispute over *moral theology* <note>original: *Zedeleer*</note>; which they, as the *Jansenists* say, completely corrupt and falsify. Furthermore, they also disagree with the *Dominicans* regarding certain sentiments and customs that the *Jesuit missionaries* allowed to the newly converted in *China*, as they believed these could coexist with the *Christian religion*, but which the *Dominicans* rejected as superstitious and *pagan* <note>A reference to the "Chinese Rites controversy" regarding whether ancestral veneration was a secular or religious act</note>; not to mention other conflicts between them and the *Benedictines*, *Theatines*, and between the Fathers of the *Oratory*: they have also been fiercely attacked by some of their fellow believers, such as *Paschasius*, *Pascal* <note>Blaise Pascal, whose *Provincial Letters* (1656) were a famous critique of Jesuit ethics</note>, *Scioppius*, *Arnauld*, and others, and depicted in a very ugly light in their writings. Meanwhile, this *Society* has always been protected by the Pope because of the services they have rendered to the *Roman Church*.

From that time on, a separate assembly of nuns appeared, which from time to time spread through many parts of *Europe*, and mostly in *Germany*. As they sought to follow the *Jesuits* in all things, they also established various high and low offices after their example, and bound themselves to maintain the vows of *Poverty*, *Chastity*, and *Obedience*. Thereafter they wore a distinct dress, which they may now, however, change at their own discretion. But as all kinds of disorders were practiced among these *Jesuitesses*, *Pope Urban VIII* found it advisable to abolish this entire Society by a separate Bull <note>An official papal decree or charter</note> in the year 1630. Nevertheless, they are still found here and there, but mostly in the *Netherlands*, and also in *Cologne*, *Vienna*, *Prague*, and *Breslau*. *Thuanus book 37*. *Hoorenbeek in his Examination of the Bull of Urban VIII against the Jesuitesses. Zimmerman, Heideggerus, etc.*

OSS-BEARERS, a certain order whose clothing is a white robe, on whose left side stands a half-red and half-white Cross. These Cross-bearers are mostly found in *Bruges*, *Namur*, *Liège*, and *Huy*. In this last place they first appeared in the year 1248; their General, or *Superior*, also resides there.

->L.<-

**LECTORES** <note>Readers</note>, are among the Roman Catholic clergy the second type of the Minor Orders, who at their consecration are presented with the book from which they shall read, with these words: *Take this and be a proclaimer of God's word, so that, if you perform your office faithfully and diligently, you may receive a portion with those who have served God's word well from the beginning.* <note>The original Dutch text provides this traditional Latin formula in translation: "Neemt het en weest een verkondiger van Gods woords..."</note> At many Courts, such as in *France* and in the *Palatinate* <note>original: *de Palts*; a historical territory of the Holy Roman Empire</note>, the Readers hold a courtly office, and must read spiritual and secular matters to the Sovereign in his chambers.

**LAY BROTHERS** and **LAY SISTERS** are those in the Monasteries who have not studied and thus cannot be Fathers <note>Priests</note> or Mothers <note>Nuns/Superiors</note>.

## MINIMS, or LESSER BROTHERS
A monastic order founded by *Francis of Paola* in the year 1435 in *Calabria*, and confirmed by Pope *Sixtus IV* in the year 1473. In addition to the vows of *Poverty* and *Chastity*, they also take a vow of perpetual fasting, for which reason they dare not eat *Meat*, *Eggs*, *Butter*, *Cheese*, nor *Dairy products* <note>original: *Melkspys*</note>; they also carry no money with them, nor do they ride on a horse. In *Paris*, they were generally called *The Good Men* <note>original: *Le bons Hommes*</note>, especially the Friars of *Chaillot*, because King *Louis XI* always gave their founder *Francis* the name of *Good Man* <note>original: *Bon Homme*</note>. They wear a dark brown habit and a small woolen belt.

## MINORES <note>Clerics Regular Minor</note>
A certain order of *Regular Clerics* <note>Priests who live according to a rule (regula) in a community</note>, who descend from a *Genoese nobleman named Adorno*, and were confirmed by Pope *Paul V*. Their General resides in *Rome* in the house of *St. Lawrence*.

## MINORES CANONICI <note>Minor Clerks Regular</note>
A *religious order* that began around the year 1589 in *Naples*, and was confirmed by Pope *Gregory XIV* and Pope *Clement VIII*. They wear a coarse black habit, live mostly in *Rome*, and observe, besides the usual vows, a fourth one: namely, that they shall not strive for any offices of honor <note>High positions or titles within the church hierarchy</note>.

## MISSIONARIES
**MISSIONARIES** are certain ecclesiastical persons, or Monks, who are sent by the **Pope**, or some **Bishops**, to proclaim the *Christian faith* to the *Heathens* <note>Historically used to refer to non-Christians, particularly polytheists or those in unevangelized lands</note>, or to whom is entrusted the task of bringing the so-called *Heretics* <note>Those holding beliefs contrary to established Roman Catholic dogma</note> onto another path, and thereby to heal the schism of the *Roman Church*. There have been three particular Orders that were sent for the guidance of the *Greeks*, *Armenians*, *Jacobites*, *Nestorianen*, and other apostates <note>In this context, members of Eastern churches not in communion with Rome</note> into the realm of the *Great Lord* <note>The Ottoman Sultan</note>, namely *Capuchins*, *Jesuits*, and *Carmelites*. The first were certainly the greatest in number, having as many as 25 missions in *Turkey* alone, not to mention those they have undertaken in *Persia*, *Georgia*, *Africa*, the *Indies*, and in the kingdom of *Congo*. 

The *Capuchins* maintained twelve missionaries in the realm of the *Sultan*, such as at *Galata*, or *Pera* <note>Districts of Constantinople/Istanbul</note>, in *Constantinople*, *Smyrna*, *Scio* <note>Chios</note>, *Athens*, *Napoli di Romania* <note>Nafplio, Greece</note>, *Candia* <note>Crete</note>, *Naxos*, *Paros*, *Milo*, *Syros*, and *Custadachi*. The *Capuchins* of the *Province of Touraine* have seven in the territory of the *Turks*, namely at *Nicosia* and *Larnaca* on the island of *Cyprus*, *Aleppo*, *Grand Cairo*, *Diarbekir*, *Nineveh*, and *Babylon*. Those of *Brittany* have six, namely at *Damascus*, *Tripoli in Syria*, *Beirut* <note>original: Baruc</note>, *Sidon*, and two in the mountains of *Lebanon*. 

The *Jesuits* have ten in this region, such as at *Constantinople*, *Smyrna*, *Damascus*, *Saida* <note>original: Seide; ancient Sidon</note>, *Aleppo*, Mount *Lebanon*, *Saint-Turia*, *Scio*, *Naxos*, and *Negropont* <note>Euboea</note>. The *Carmelites* have only three in the *Ottoman Empire*, namely at *Aleppo*, *Tripoli in Syria*, and at *Basra*. On Mount *Carmel*, where there are three of these clerics,

**MI** <note>Likely referring to a specific mission location or island, possibly Milo or Mykonos, continuing from the previous page</note> is a Hermitage, and an uninhabited place. All these Missionaries understand the languages of the countries to which they are sent. Those who reside near *Constantinople*, such as in the *Archipelago* <note>The Aegean Islands</note>, *Morea* <note>The Peloponnese peninsula in Greece</note>, and *Romania* <note>Historical term for the Byzantine/Ottoman Balkans</note>, apply themselves only to the *Greek* language, and that is sufficient. The others must also master the *Arabic*, *Turkish*, and *Armenian* languages, which are in use there. They do not focus so much on changing their schisms and customs, along with their ceremonies, as they do on making them abandon their [sinful] habits, and on making them recognize the Pope as the universal Head of the Church. There are always those among them who practice the Medical Arts <note>original: "Geneeskunst"</note>, partly to make themselves agreeable thereby to the *Pashas* <note>original: "Bassaas"; high-ranking Ottoman officials</note> and other great men of that land, so that they might be protected by their authority against those of other faiths. In the 18th century, some *Lutherans* also allowed themselves to be used as Missionaries to Heathen and unbelieving places; to which end several students from *Halle* <note>A center of Lutheran Pietism in Germany</note>, under the protection of the King of *Denmark*, went to *Tranquebar* in the *East Indies* <note>A Danish trading colony in Tamil Nadu, India</note> to convert the *Malabarians* <note>The Tamil-speaking people of the region</note> and other nations there to the Christian faith.

**OLIVETANS**, in Latin *Monks of Saint Mary of Mount Olivet* <note>original: "Monachi St. Mariæ Montis Oliveti"</note>, are certain monks who are dressed entirely in white, yet in most other matters, they follow the rule of *Saint Benedict*. They have many monasteries, including one in *Rome* near the Church of *Saint Mary the New* <note>original: "St. Maria Nuova"</note> in the *Boarian Forum* <note>original: "foro Boario"; the ancient cattle market</note>, or *Campo Vaccino* <note>original: "Vaccino"; the "Cow Pasture," a common name for the Roman Forum in the 17th-18th centuries</note>. The head monastery of their order, holding the title of an Abbey, is located between *Siena* and *Pienza* on a mountain named *Mount Oliveto*. The founder was *Johannes Tolomei*, around the year 1320, who later took the name *Bernard*, a nobleman from *Siena*. He dedicated himself to spiritual and secular laws <term>canon and civil law</term>, obtained a doctorate in them, and taught them publicly in *Siena*. After some time, he was afflicted with a severe inflammation of the eyes, which moved him to make a special vow to the Blessed Virgin *Mary*, should she deign to help him again. After his wish was granted, he set out with the intention of leading an austere life to one of his estates called *Accona*, near *Mount Elcino* <note>likely Montalcino</note>, in the company of two other noblemen from *Siena*, one of whom was named *Patricio Patricius* and the other *Ambrose Piccolomini*. ## P.

### ORDER OF ST. PAUL,

otherwise also called *Minims* <note>original: *Minimi*, meaning "the least"</note>, originated around the year 1450 from *Francis*, born in *Paola*, a city in *Calabria*, from which they also received this name. There are also *Hermits of St. Paul*, a religious order which has *Paul the Hermit* as its Patron, and was introduced in 1215 by *Eusebius of Gran* <note>modern Esztergom</note> in *Hungary*; they also received the Rule of *St. Augustine* from Pope *Clement V* in the year 1308. Around the year 1363, this order was renewed by *Paul*, Bishop of *Veszprém*, and it possessed many monasteries in *Hungary*, which were nevertheless destroyed by the *Turks*. There is another Congregation of *Hermits of St. Paul* established in the year 1553 in *Spain* and *Italy*.

->R.<-

**RECOLLECTS**, or *Minorites of St. Francis* <note>The Minorites are the Friars Minor</note>, a certain brotherhood of Roman Monks, established in the year 1530. **REGULARS** <term>Regulares: From the Latin "regula" (rule); clergy who live in a community according to a specific religious rule.</term>, are clergy in the Roman Church who follow a certain Rule of an Order toward perfection, and distinguish themselves from others by a specific dress. There are actually only four types of Rules approved in the Roman Church, under one of which all religious groups place themselves: namely, the Rule of *St. Basil*, *St. Augustine*, *St. Benedict*, and *Francis*. This is because the *Carthusians* and *Jesuits* have their own statutes as a Rule, and therefore [according to some] do not belong among the Regular Monks. Likewise, those are called Regular Benefices <note>A church office that provides an income or "living" to the holder.</note> which, according to their institutions, cannot be given to any others but Regular Clerks.

Later, a congregation of the *Hermits of Saint Paul* was established in *France* and in *Spain*.

## THE Religious Orders

...monks in the Roman Church, whom the Pope appointed over the Hospital of *St. Mary in Saxia* <note>original: "St. Maria in Saxia"; this refers to the hospital of Santo Spirito in Sassia in Rome, one of the oldest in the world.</note> in *Rome*, to raise and care for the foundlings <note>Infants abandoned by their parents and taken in by charitable institutions.</note> there. They wear a double white cross on the left side of their black habit and cloak, according to the rule of *St. Augustine*, and are under a Commander appointed by the Pope.

**ORDER OF THE HOLY TRINITY** <note>original: "ST. TRINITATIS ORDO"</note> is a religious order in the Roman Church that emerged around the year 1209, and was established to ransom prisoners from slavery <note>The Trinitarians were specifically founded to buy back Christians captured by pirates or held in North Africa.</note>. The monks of this order in *Spain* wear a white habit along with a brown hood, and on both sides a red and blue cross; those in *France* dress entirely in white, except that they wear the same kind of cross as the former.

**SECULAR PRIESTS** <note>original: "SECULARES SACERDOTES"</note> are clergy in the Roman Church who have not bound themselves to any monastic vows and do not live in a fixed religious order <note>Unlike "regular" clergy who follow a specific Rule (regula), secular priests serve in the community or "the world" (saeculum).</note>.

**SERVITES** or **SERVANTS OF THE BLESSED VIRGIN** <note>original: "SERVI BEATÆ VIRGINIS"</note>, meaning *Servants of the Blessed Virgin*, is a certain religious order founded around the year 1232 in *Florence* by seven noble and wealthy men, among whom *Bonfilius dei Monaldi* <note>The Dutch text lists "Bonfebius de Monaldis," a variant of Bonfilius, one of the Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order.</note>, or as others suggest, *Blessed Bonavitus*, was the most prominent. There was also a society of these servants of the Holy Virgin founded in *Marseille* in the year 1257, who lived according to the rule of *St. Augustine*.

**THEATINES** <note>original: "THEATYNEN"</note> are monks and *Clerics Regular* <note>Priests who live according to a religious rule (regula) rather than as secular clergy.</note> in *Rome*, founded by *Gian Pietro Carafa* <note>original: "Johannes Petrus Caraffa".</note>, Bishop of *Theate* (or *Chieti*) in the Kingdom of *Naples*, who afterwards became Pope under the name *Paul IV*. After he had been employed in several embassies, Emperor *Charles V* gave him the Bishopric of *Brindisi*, which he not only refused, but moreover he abandoned everything he possessed and went into a wilderness; there, with the permission of Pope *Clement VII* in the year 1523, he made his vows in *Rome*.

He was joined by *Gaetano* <note>Saint Cajetan (1480–1547).</note>, Count of *Thiene*, who was later canonized; *Marcello Cajetano*; *Bonifacio de' Colli* <note>original: "Bonifacius Collenfis".</note>; and *Paolo Consiglieri* <note>original: "Paulus Confiliarius".</note>. They wished to adopt the lifestyle of the *Apostles*, to possess nothing as their own, and to demand no alms, but to be content with whatever was given to them voluntarily. After this, they were also received in *Venice* in the year 1527 and in *Naples* in 1530. Subsequently, this assembly became very prestigious, and many learned men have sprung from it. Cardinal *Mazarin* introduced them to *Paris* and bought them a house next to the *Louvre*, into which they moved in the year 1648. **THOMISTS and SCOTISTS** are two entirely opposing factions within the Roman Catholic Church. The Scotists take their origin from *John Duns*, called *Scotus* <note>John Duns Scotus (c. 1266–1308), a hugely influential Franciscan philosopher and theologian.</note>, and teach that the *Holy Virgin was conceived and born without sin* <note>This refers to the doctrine of the Immaculate Conception.</note>, an opinion which the Franciscans and Jesuits support. The head of the Thomists was *Thomas Aquinas* <note>The Italian Dominican friar and "Doctor of the Church" (1225–1274).</note>, and these teach that the *Virgin Mary was indeed conceived and born in sin*. This struggle has lasted in the Roman Church for over 300 years, and the Popes held back their verdict for as long as was feasible, because they did not wish to offend <note>original: "voor het hoofd stooten"; literally "to hit against the head."</note> either of these powerful factions. Finally, Pope *Alexander VII* pronounced the verdict in favor of the Scotists in the *Year 1661*, by which the Thomists (or Dominicans) were greatly offended; they not only persist in their opinion despite the Papal verdict, but also harbor a great hatred toward their opposing party because of it.
